$comment: Annotated example for run_handoff_sessions.ps1, showing EVERY field.
You almost certainly do not want to start from this file — run `-Init` in your
repo instead, which writes a minimal config with your git root and branch
already detected. Come here to look a field up.
This example is the downstream project A wave-3 run the script was generalised from,
so every field below has actually been used in anger. Fields marked OPTIONAL
SECRETS NEVER GO IN THIS FILE. It is meant to be committed. Tokens are read
from `envFrom` at preflight and exported to the child sessions.
$comment_repo: OPTIONAL, and best omitted. The runner detects the git root, so leaving this
out keeps the committed config free of any machine-specific path. Set it only
to drive a repository other than the one you are standing in.
$comment_launcher: The session tool, as a SWAPPABLE ADAPTER. Defaults describe Claude Code, so an
unedited config just works; override only the keys you need — the block merges
key by key, so replacing `command` does not lose list/logs/stop.
{{prompt}} is substituted as exactly ONE argument, never split or re-expanded
ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING in `start`: --allowedTools is variadic and swallows
everything up to the next flag, so a prompt placed after it becomes another
'tool name' and the session starts with NO task. Keep {{tools}} before

$comment_worktrees: Both default sensibly: parent directory of `repo`, and repo's own folder name.
$comment_linkDirs: Directories junctioned from the main checkout into every worktree, instead of
being copied or regenerated. Use for generated artifacts that must stay single:
a graphify graph, a model cache. Skipped silently if absent in the main checkout.
$comment_copyDirs: Directories COPIED from the main checkout into every worktree, so each session
owns an independent instance it may rebuild or append to without touching the
others' - a gitignored working ledger, a per-worktree code graph. linkDirs = one
shared artifact; copyDirs = one artifact per session. Skipped silently if absent.
$comment_copyFiles: Single FILES copied from the main checkout into every worktree - the gitignored
.env with the secrets and switches the app reads from its own root, so a worktree
session neither generates a fresh DB key nor binds a different port. Skipped if absent.
Per-session variants: a session may carry its own linkDirs / copyDirs / copyFiles,
merged AFTER the global lists (see session E below). That is how one lane links the
live data directory while every other worktree stays unable to reach it.
$comment_postWorktree: Runs once per newly created worktree, in the configured shell, with {{vars}}
expanded. A fresh worktree is an UNAPPROVED folder: the first session in it
asks to trust the directory and its hooks, and a background session cannot
answer — it goes `blocked` and stays there. Pre-approve it here.
Pass --no-env when the adopting repo resolves its .env back to the main checkout: the
worktree .env this script would write otherwise pre-empts that resolution silently.
postWorktree: & '{{python}}' '{{skillDir}}\trust_worktree.py' '{{worktree}}' --repo '{{repo}}' --mcpjson omnigraph; Push-Location '{{worktree}}'; uv sync --frozen 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 1; Pop-Location
$comment_vars: Free-form passthrough available to briefs, guards and postWorktree as
{{name}}. Values may themselves reference the built-ins: session, key,
sessionName, model, worktree, branch, repo, baseBranch, stateDir, and
skillDir (the folder this skill lives in - it ships trust_worktree.py, the
pre-approval helper postWorktree above calls; nothing repo-specific needed).
A worktree holds TRACKED files only: no venv, no generated graph, no ignored
workspace. postWorktree is where each of those is created per worktree - a
session that runs the main checkout's venv from a worktree imports the MAIN
checkout's package (its editable install points there), silently.
$comment_subagents: OPT-IN. Rendered into every brief as {{subagentPolicy}}, so all sessions delegate
the same way and the policy is stated exactly once. Omit the block and briefs say
nothing about subagents — a session told to delegate with no cap and no tier
leafRule (default true) stops subagents spawning subagents; without it a wave fans
out geometrically and the budget is gone before the work is.
maxDepth (default 3) sets the delegation hierarchy: Main orchestrator -> phase-specific
orchestrator subagent -> task-specific subagent orchestrator. Level 3 subagents are leaves.
$comment_sessions: One entry per handoff. `model` is required. `name` defaults to the lowercased
key and decides the branch and worktree names. Each needs `brief` (inline) or
A session may set its own "launcher" (an adapter name or an object, same shapes as the
top-level one) to drive a different agent for that lane — mechanical and verification lanes
on a second provider spread the quota; judgement lanes stay on the first.
$comment_resources_guardsOnly: resources: what a session HOLDS while running, as name or name:read / name:write (bare =
write). The runner will not start a session whose resources conflict with a RUNNING one:
write excludes everything on that name, read excludes only write. Ordering (dependsOn) is
not exclusion - a reader once starved the writer of a single-holder store.
guardsOnly: no agent is launched; the session cuts a worktree at the base branch's HEAD
and runs the guards there - the pinned, idle final suite. It needs no brief.
machineBudget (below) is ADVISORY: rendered into briefs as {{machineBudget}} with the path
of <stateDir>/load.json, which the runner refreshes every poll (cpu_percent,
running_sessions). A runner that blocked on CPU would deadlock behind another project.
$comment_controllerBrief: OPTIONAL. The orchestrator's own brief, rendered FIRST by -EmitBriefs with {{stateFile}},
worktree, attach command and DONE note), so a controller session can be restarted from
the same source of truth as its lanes.
$comment_lanes: Lanes run in PARALLEL; sessions inside a lane run in SEQUENCE. Put sessions
that contend for a resource in the same lane. Omit `lanes` entirely and every
session gets its own lane (maximum parallelism).
Here: E writes the store and A follows it; D and B only read, so they share a lane.
`dependsOn` is the cross-lane primitive: G's lane WAITS until A and B have merged,
then cuts its worktree from the base branch that carries them. A dependency that
ends without merging (guards red, conflict, blocked) stops G's lane instead of
leaving it polling all night. maxDependencyHours (default 48) bounds the wait.
$comment_briefTemplate: Wrapped around each session's brief; {{brief}} is where the session body lands.
This is the DRY seam: the rules every session shares are written ONCE here, and
each session file carries only its own task. Use briefTemplateFile to keep it
in a markdown file instead of this JSON.
$comment_guards: OPT-IN. Omit the whole block and the runner merges on a clean stop alone.
Fully generic: any command. `{{guards}}` in args expands in place to `paths`.
$comment_allowedTools: Headless sessions cannot answer permission prompts, so tools are pre-allowed.
The repo's hooks still run on every call — the hook, not the prompt, is the guard.
NOTE: playwright's tool prefix depends on how it is wired. User-scope server =
$comment_preflight: requirePaths are checked before anything starts. envFrom is a JSON file whose
`env` block is exported to the child sessions — secrets stay in the main
checkout and are never copied into a worktree.
$comment_traps: OPTIONAL. Rendered into every brief as {{traps}} under a 'measured traps - do not
re-measure' heading, so a trap one session paid for reaches every later one.
traps: Serena's replace_symbol_body drops decorators on the symbol it replaces - re-add them and diff.
PowerShell parameter and variable names are case-insensitive: a local $doneFile IS the -DoneFile parameter.
A worktree's python must be the worktree's own venv; the main checkout's editable install imports the main checkout's src.
$comment_finish: quietMinutes: a session whose DONE note exists, whose branch is clean and has had no
commit for this long is FINISHED even if the agents view still says working (measured:
three hours of that, twice). stopAfterMerge: stop the finished session once merged, so
its process releases the worktree folder.
$comment_stall: THE STALL WATCHDOG. quietMinutes only ever closes a session that ALREADY wrote its
DONE note; stallMinutes ends one that is hung BEFORE writing one. Measured
2026-09-12: an agy child sat 48 min with an empty stdout, no commit and no DONE
note, and the lane waited for the launcher's own --print-timeout of 360 min.
A session counts as stalled only when ALL THREE of its log, its worktree and its
process tree have been quiet that long - the same day, an agy child that looked
identical from outside for 35 min was working and finished normally, so two
signals would have killed real work. 0 disables the watchdog.
stallWindow is the RATE RULE: maxStalls stalls inside `hours` hours means a
general problem rather than a one-off, so the lane stops for the operator
(status: stalled-repeatedly) instead of being resumed a sixth time. Stalls older
than the window drop out of the count.
